title: Ops Scribe: compile runbooks into small reusable adminlets
creator: Anika Rao
description: Problem: Operator runbooks are long, freeform, and difficult to version, test, and compose for quick remediation. Goal: Implement an 'Ops Scribe' compiler that converts canonical runbook steps into compact, typed adminlets (small idempotent actions) that can be invoked by runbook runners, the support UI, and automated remediators. The compiler should emit a metadata manifest, a typed input schema, a safety policy reference, and an execution shim that integrates with the admin runtime. This ticket covers the first-pass compiler, a minimal adminlet registry, and end-to-end demo with a synthetic incident scenario.
acceptance_criteria: A compiler binary (or server) converts a YAML/Markdown runbook into one or more adminlet packages
Each adminlet package contains: name, semantic id, input schema (OpenAPI-lite), safety policy id, and a versioned execution shim
Runbook runner can fetch an adminlet from the registry and execute it in a sandboxed mode with recorded provenance
Adminlet invocation produces structured telemetry (start/stop, tokens consumed, errors) and appears in Console traces
Two sample runbooks are converted and used in a demo: 'rotate-redis-credentials' and 'evict-slow-worker'
Security review completed for execution shim and the registry access model
implementation_notes: Compiler input: existing canonical runbook markdown with explicit 'step:' frontmatter; fallback heuristics when missing
Output format: zip package with manifest.json (flat key-value), schema.json (JSON Schema v2020-12 subset), shim.py (or shim.js) with a uniform adapter API
Registry: S3-backed blob store + Dynamo-like index for lookups by semantic id and version; initially read-write restricted to ops service account
Execution shim: run in ephemeral container (gvisor) or a restricted process with capability drops; no network by default unless policy permits
Telemetry: emit trace id, adminlet id/version, duration_ms, exit_code, and an optional 'notes' field for operator text
Testing: unit tests for parser heuristics + integration test that runs demo adminlets against a staging cluster emulation
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement compiler MVP and local registry; convert two canonical runbooks; demo with SREs
Phase 1 (staging): deploy registry behind VPC, wire Console to show adminlet traces, run integration tests with staging clusters
Phase 2 (canary): enable read-only access to adminlets in a subset of oncall flows; collect metrics and operator feedback
Phase 3 (general): full registry access, docs in Confluence, add CLI 'scribe convert' to dev tooling
telemetry_and_slo: Emit events to runtime-traces with tag 'adminlet:ops-scribe'
SLO: adminlet compile success rate >= 99% for non-malformed runbooks
SLO: average adminlet execution latency under simulated load < 2s for shim startup (excluding underlying remediation)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental privilege escalation via shims. Mitigation: minimal runtime privileges, mandatory security review, and runtime policy enforcement
Risk: inconsistent schema extraction from freeform runbooks. Mitigation: conservative defaults, validation failures surface during compile and block registry publish
Risk: operator reliance on automated adminlets without understanding side effects. Mitigation: require explicit 'can_auto_run' flag and audit trail for any automated invocations
